run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T01:41:23Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy tracks an error rise that starts around 01:48 and is caused by failures of the ad service's GetAds call, which is targeted every minute by Chaos Mesh JVM fault experiments. frontend-proxy error spans appear on both 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' and rise together from a 0.005-0.017/s baseline (01:24-01:47) to ~1.0-1.99/s by 02:00. Inside the frontend only ad-dependent operations error (GET, GET /api/data, 'executing api route (pages) /api/data', grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds); /api/cart, /api/checkout, CartService and CheckoutService spans show 0/s errors. The ad service's own server span oteldemo.AdService/GetAds carries STATUS_CODE_ERROR from 01:48:30 onward while its non-error ad traffic collapses from ~0.95/s to ~0.07/s, and its pod logs show repeated gRPC 'Exception while executing runnable ...' lines. Chaos Mesh events in namespace chaos-mesh show Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-return spawning a JVMChaos object every minute from 01:47:02, each logging 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/ad-554b849958-sk6fg/ad' and recovering ~50-55 s later; the error onset follows the first applications. The ad pod is Running with 0 restarts, low CPU (~0.01-0.02 core/s) and smooth memory growth, and the flagd ad fault flags are stored as 'off', so resource exhaustion and the demo adFailure flag are not supported. The exact JVMChaos spec (action/method/value) and the alert rule expression could not be read, and the alert startsAt (01:41:23) precedes the large error-rate rise.

claims.text: frontend-proxy ERROR-status span rate (5m) was low but non-zero at 01:24-01:47 (0.0074-0.0167 per second), then rose from 0.337/s at 01:48:23 to 1.04/s at 01:50:23, ~1.73/s at 01:54:23, ~1.99/s at 01:58:23 and was still 0.87/s at 02:01:23.

frontend-proxy's error spans are the operations 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress'; both move together from 01:48:23 (0.178/s and 0.159/s) to peaks of ~1.00/s and ~0.99/s at 01:58:23, so the proxy's ingress errors track its egress calls to the frontend.

In the frontend service, error-status spans are confined to GET, GET /api/data, 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (each ~0.16/s at 01:48:23 rising to ~0.98/s at 01:58:23), while GET/POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, CartService/AddItem, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and tcp.connect error rates are 0/s throughout the window.

The ad service's own server span oteldemo.AdService/GetAds carries STATUS_CODE_ERROR from the 01:50:23 point (0.399/s) up to 0.985/s at 01:58:23 and 0.429/s at 02:01:23, while ad GetAds spans with no error status fall from ~0.95/s at 01:24-01:47 to 0.133/s at 01:58:23 and 0.067/s at 02:01:23; ad's flagd spans (ResolveBoolean, flagd EventStream) stay at 0-0.004/s error.

Ad-service error onset: the 2-minute rate of ad ERROR spans is 0 for every point from 01:40:00 to 01:48:00, first becomes non-zero at 01:48:30 (0.011/s), then 0.64/s at 01:49:00 and 1.10/s at 01:49:30.

Chaos Mesh Schedule events in namespace chaos-mesh show Schedule 'otel-demo-ad-jvm-return' spawning a new JVMChaos object every minute: 'Create new object: otel-demo-ad-jvm-return-gbjlm' at 01:47:02, then -9f6n6 01:48:02, -j2fmx 01:49:02, -plmnp 01:50:02, -ljkwf 01:51:02, -dlm4f 01:52:02, -4x48z 01:53:02, -m8wnc 01:54:02, -gzz89 01:55:02, -2xnmj 01:56:02.

Each JVMChaos experiment reports 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/ad-554b849958-sk6fg/ad' (Applied at 01:47:12, 01:48:06, 01:49:06, 01:50:04, 01:51:04, 01:52:06, 01:53:04, 01:54:04, 01:55:04) and 'Successfully recover chaos for otel-demo/ad-554b849958-sk6fg/ad' about 50-55 s later (e.g. Applied 01:48:06, Recovered 01:48:58).

The ad pod ad-554b849958-sk6fg is Running with restartCount 0 and startTime 2026-11-18T01:11:07Z (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad), and all 21 pods returned for namespace otel-demo are Running with 0 restarts, so the failure is not a crash or restart.

The ad container's logs contain repeated 'Exception while executing runnable io.grpc.internal.ServerImpl$JumpToApplicationThreadServerStreamListener$1HalfClosed@...' lines interleaved with normal 'Targeted ad request received ...' lines across 01:54:07-01:56:17 (120 of 453 matching lines in a 120 s slice).

Event grouping across all namespaces for the window shows only chaos-mesh JVMChaos/Schedule events (9 Applied, 10 Started, 9 Recovered, 9 TimeUp, 55 Updated, 10 Spawned) plus data-recorders Deployment/Job/Pod/PVC/StatefulSet events; no otel-demo Pod events appear in that view.

The frontend-proxy error series in this Prometheus has samples only from 01:30:00 onward in a 24-hour query: 10-minute error rate 0.009/s at 01:30:00, 0.005/s at 01:40:00, 0.342/s at 01:50:00 and 1.255/s at 02:00:00, so no baseline exists before 01:30.

The ad container shows no resource saturation: CPU rate is ~0.005-0.010 core/s before 01:48 and only ~0.010-0.022 core/s after 01:48, and memory working set grows smoothly from 322 MB (01:25) to 365 MB (02:00); this does not support a CPU-stress or memory-exhaustion cause for the ad failures.

The flagd ConfigMap flagd-config stores the ad fault flags with defaultVariant 'off' (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc all 'off'), and ad's flagd evaluation spans show ~0 errors, which does not support the feature-flag adFailure injection as the active cause.

The fault mechanism is Chaos Mesh JVM fault injection into the ad container: applying 'chaos for otel-demo/ad-554b849958-sk6fg/ad' from the otel-demo-ad-jvm-return schedule makes oteldemo.AdService/GetAds return errors (ad ERROR spans and the ad pod's gRPC 'Exception while executing runnable' log lines), which makes the frontend's GET /api/data fail (grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds client-span errors), which produces frontend and frontend-proxy ingress errors and the RequestErrorRate alert; the timing matches, with error onset ~01:48:20 following the first JVMChaos applications at 01:47:12 and 01:48:06.

Because the schedule and its experiments are named 'otel-demo-ad-jvm-return', the injected JVMChaos action is plausibly a method 'return' (method-level fault) applied to the ad service's GetAds path, but the experiment spec could not be read, so the action, target class/method and injected value remain unverified.

The alert's startsAt of 01:41:23, earlier than the 01:48:20 error-rate rise, is plausibly explained by the alert condition being error rate above 0, tripping on the pre-existing sporadic error rate observed from 01:30 to 01:47; the rule expression could not be read to confirm this.
Rejected: the ad failures come from the demo feature flag adFailure (or adHighCpu/adManualGc) served by flagd - the stored flagd flags are 'off' and flagd evaluation spans show no errors.

Rejected: cart, checkout or payment failures explain the frontend errors - the frontend's cart/checkout client spans (CartService/GetCart, CartService/AddItem, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder) and the /api/cart and /api/checkout routes show 0/s error rate for the whole window.

Stop the fault by suspending or deleting the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-return (and any still-running JVMChaos experiments it spawned), then confirm that oteldemo.AdService/GetAds error spans and frontend-proxy ingress error rate return to the ~0.005-0.017/s background level observed before 01:47.
Inspect the JVMChaos/Schedule spec through the Chaos Mesh controller (action, target class/method, duration, mode) since those fields were not readable with the available resource kinds.

gaps: The JVMChaos and Schedule custom resources (namespace chaos-mesh, names otel-demo-ad-jvm-return and otel-demo-ad-jvm-return-*) could not be read because those kinds are not queryable here, so the injected action, target class/method, injected value, duration and mode are unverified.

The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not present in the registered Prometheus (a rule_name=RequestErrorRate query returned no rules with status no_data), so the alert expression, its evaluation window and the reported current value 2.1111 could not be verified.

Jaeger returned no traces for service frontend-proxy over 01:40:00-02:05:17 and none for frontend over 01:45:00-02:05:17 (both views status no_data), so span-level error messages, gRPC status codes and parent references for these traces are unknown.
The frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-zsgq9 returned no log lines for 01:45:00-02:05:17 (status no_data), so frontend-side error text was not observed.

A query for 'Exception' in the ad pod logs over 01:15:00-01:45:00 returned no lines with status no_data, so 'no such exceptions before the incident' is not asserted; only their presence during the incident is established, and the ad pod logs view of 01:55:50-01:56:17 was itself incomplete (newest 80 of 2317 lines).
Whether the schedule kept spawning experiments after 01:56:02 is unknown; the newest chaos-mesh event in the returned view is 01:56:02.
The creator of the Schedule and any prior change history are unknown; the change_history integration is not available in this Run.

No error-status span series were returned for otel-demo services cart, checkout, payment, accounting, currency, email, product-catalog, quote, shipping, kafka or image-provider; this shows only that no such series matched, not that their error rate was zero.
Sporadic low-level error rates on fraud-detection (0.0036-0.0048/s) and recommendation (0.0037/s) exist both before and after the onset and are not tied by evidence to this incident.
next_steps: Suspend the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-ad-jvm-return and confirm recovery of ad GetAds error spans and frontend-proxy ingress errors.
Read the JVMChaos/Schedule spec and the Chaos Mesh controller logs to determine the exact injected method/action and who created the schedule at about 01:46-01:47.
Review the RequestErrorRate rule (not present in this Prometheus) to confirm its expression, window and whether a >0 threshold is appropriate given the ~0.005-0.017/s background error rate.
